headers.//: INERT ON FIREBASE. Firebase Hosting runs its own transport compression and overrides Content-Encoding on pre-compressed files -- it served framework.js.br with no encoding at all and data.br as gzip, which fed Unity raw brotli as JS. That is why webGLDecompressionFallback is ON: Unity decompresses in JS and Firebase's compression becomes harmless. These rules only matter on a host that leaves pre-compressed files alone, e.g. serve.py.

Content-Type must describe the file INSIDE the compression, not the .br wrapper.

Build files are hash-named (webGLNameFilesAsHashes), so immutable is safe. This glob must NOT overlap the no-cache rules below -- precedence between overlapping header globs is not something to rely on.
